messages.subject: Predict function and covariate scaling
parts:
This might be an incredibly simple question but for background I am running occuFP models on bat survey data comparing two detection methods and also analyzing state variables influencing occupancy that are mostly metrics that I have scaled.

My question is when I am creating the data frame to use the predict function to estimate detection probability between methods, should I use the scaled mean of continuous variables, which would be very near 0, or the mean of the original values? 

This is the code for setting values to the scaled mean of 0 - 

> methodnd<-data.frame(Method=factor(c("MistNet","Acoustics")), Density=0, GSS_NP=0)
> predict(bdetm02, newdata=methodnd, type="det", appendData=TRUE)

Thank you in advance for any assistance.

messages.author: 02d195331194f5bd
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Predict function and covariate scaling
parts: Correct. You want the data exactly like the data in your model. So if the data in your model is scaled, then you want the data in your new data to be scaled (using the same mean and standard deviation as your original data). If you just want to predict at the mean of scaled covariates, then you can just set the covariates equal to zero. If you want to predict across the whole range of covariate values you observed, then you can do a sequence from the minimum scaled covariate value to the maximum scaled covariate value (in which case you probably want to use the function expand.grid() instead of data.frame().)
